messages:
Maya T.: Drafting an alternative to the big role modal: a compact "pill-ladder" inline picker in the roles matrix. Visual idea: a stacked pill for each seat type that expands into a vertical ladder on hover/focus. Reason: keep context, faster bulk edits, fewer modals. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc/pill-ladder-proto :sparkles:

Jin S.: Nice. Couple things: when the ladder expands, how do we avoid layout shift for long org names? maybe use an overlay rather than expand the cell. Also need a clear affordance for "this action sends an email" vs "this is a local role set".

Maya T.: Good point. Proposal: overlay anchored to the cell with a subtle backdrop. Two actions inside: "Set role" (no email) and "Invite & set role" (sends invite). Microcopy will surface that difference.

Noor H.: Copy suggestion: use verbs that match intent. "Set role" vs "Invite and grant" vs "Promote" felt ambiguous. My picks: "Set role" (in-org), "Invite & add" (external). Keep CTA verbs short.

Aran K.: Keyboard/a11y: overlay must be part of tab order, Esc closes, arrow keys move between pills, Enter confirms. Also, for screen readers include descriptive labels like "Set role to Power for Jordan (no email)".

Samira R.: Accessibility nits: ensure the overlay has role=dialog and is modal to SRs (trap focus). If we use overlay, provide visible focus ring on each pill with >=4.5:1 contrast. Also, aria-live region for success toasts (polite).

Maya T.: On billing, we need to show cost impact inline. Idea: tiny cost chip under the pill: e.g., "+1 seat (billed)" or "no seat change". That should be linked to billing docs with aria-describedby.

Jin S.: UX edge-case: SSO enforced roles. Show a lock icon on pills that cannot be changed; clicking should show the enforcement note with link to org SSO settings. For keyboard users, locked pills should be aria-disabled and the reason available via aria-describedby.

Noor H.: Audit concerns: when role changes happen via the picker, include method in the audit record: event = "role.assignment", method = "picker-inline". Also include a preview link that opens the audit panel filtered to that user. That will help support traces.

DesignBot: sample audit row for UI:
```
{ "event": "role.assignment", "actor": "jin.s@redwood.com", "target": "alex@acme.com", "from": "Read-only", "to": "Power", "method": "picker-inline", "ts": "2025-04-02T11:03:08Z" }
```
This can be deep-linked from the role cell to the right-hand audit rail.

Aran K.: Undo flow: show an ephemeral toast with "Changed Alex to Power  Undo" (aria-live=polite). Undo should be accessible by keyboard (focusable) and survive quick nav. Also consider a 10s grace window before finalizing billing changes.

Samira R.: Contrast again: action pills when selected must have distinct border + fill; test with both light/dark and high contrast modes. For tooltips use aria-describedby and ensure they appear on focus.

Maya T.: Checklist to hand to eng: 
- pill-ladder component (overlay, keyboard arrow nav, escape to close)
- ARIA: dialog semantics for overlay, aria-disabled for SSO locks, aria-describedby for billing/tooltips
- copy: "Set role" vs "Invite & add"; undo toast text as above
- billing hint chip + link to docs; include 10s billing grace for seat-affecting changes
- audit: emit structured `role.assignment` entries (method: "picker-inline") and deep-link to audit rail
- visuals: 4.5:1 contrast for selected state; visible focus outline

Maya T.: Assigning follow-ups: @Aran K. can you draft keyboard keymap and focus trap behavior? @Samira R. please run Figma a11y pass once available. @Noor H. can you finalize copy variants.

Aran K.: I'll push a keyboard map and state machine tonight.

Samira R.: Will test with NVDA + VoiceOver and report issues.

Noor H.: I'll add 3 copy variants for product review and include examples for toast and tooltip.

DesignBot: Updated prototype link: https://www.figma.com/file/abc/pill-ladder-proto?node-id=22:7  component id `comp_pill_14`.

Maya T.: Thanks everyone  we're slotting this for design review Wednesday. Short agenda: accessibility pass, copy review, audit deep-link behavior.
